gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-meroi: Noto Sans Meroitic reads approachably, its lowercase filling the line almost like capitals. Noto Sans Meroitic keeps a long passage friendly, while Capture It lays down a single-width trail like a rolling-ball pen.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-modi: Noto Sans Modi lets daylight into every curve, with lowercase sitting close to capital height. And a longer passage in it goes down smoothly, a quiet foil to the urban Capture It, whose y has a tail as thick as its arm.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-mono: Tall, tough and urban: Capture It draws every stroke at a single thickness, with letters nearly sealed shut. Noto Sans Mono does the opposite job, spacing its sturdy lowercase generously so every curve stays open.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-mro: Bent-paperclip strokes, towering and tight: that is Capture It, with no thick-thin shifts anywhere. But Noto Sans Mro opens wide entrances into every letter, so a longer passage stays dense and tall yet inviting.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-multa: Noto Sans Multani reads modern, its lofty x-height and wide-gapped e giving each line a lifted look. Noto Sans Multani can go a touch smaller than you would guess, since Capture It's tubular, copper-pipe strokes keep the top end loud.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-myanm: Noto Sans Myanmar forms a thick, heavy-looking strip through the middle of each line, with a broadly welcoming c. A long read feels solid yet clear next to Capture It's tight, towering shapes.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-nabat: Noto Sans Nabataean stands its lowercase almost cap-tall, with wide-open s curves. And a longer passage keeps that lofty rhythm, while Capture It cuts its sealed-up strokes like a fixed-width router bit.
